stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
Harness edits (context/harness/). All trace to the single available rollout, context/rollouts/base1.md, which completed both deliverables but exhibited the failures below.

1. context/harness/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md (was empty) — three tool-use rules.

   a. Bounded fallback for missing-binary helper failures. Moment: base1.md:255-313 — the agent ran `python3 scripts/read_doc.py` on home-study-report.docx, client-intake-memo.docx, and guardianship-order.docx in sequence; every call failed with the identical `FileNotFoundError: 'podman'` traceback, and only after the third identical failure did it fall back (base1.md:315-331), where python-docx extracted all three immediately. This is the earliest divergence in the run: the documented `read` path (systemprompt.md) handles .docx natively and was bypassed. The rule encodes the verified workspace facts (read_doc.py's podman sandbox is unusable in this workspace; python-docx installed; `read` is the documented path) plus the one-bounded-fallback-then-stop discipline, so this class of failure costs one call instead of three plus a diagnosis turn.

   b. Sequential same-file edits. Moment: base1.md:1232-1282 — four `edit` calls to build_docs.py issued in one turn each reported "Edit applied successfully", yet grep showed only the last had survived (agent's own diagnosis at base1.md:1268: "Parallel edits raced — last write won"); it then re-applied three edits and did an extra rebuild/revalidate cycle. Recorded as an environment tool-loop fact: same-file edits race and silently keep only the last; re-check the file after a batch.

   c. Capped-output completeness. Moment: base1.md:319-322 vs 537-663 — the docx extraction observation was capped and saved to a 258-line file; the agent re-read only lines 1-120 and relied on the inline preview for the remainder, leaving the home-study certification tail unread. Rule: the saved file is the complete output; read it with offset before treating a source as fully read.

2. context/harness/guardrails.md (was empty) — two standing rules.

   a. Artifacts before budget risk. Moment: base1.md:848-903 — immediately after writing a 43KB build script containing the full text of both documents, the run hit a mid-task summary/continuation boundary whose own status block said "NOT YET DONE: Execute build_docs.py"; output/ was confirmed empty at base1.md:914-919. The budget held this time, but at that moment zero requested files existed on disk — a risk visible but not realised. Rule: build and verify the first artifact once its content exists, before investing context in the next.

   b. Post-validate usability recheck. Moment: base1.md:943-948 vs 1248 — `validate.py` returned "OK" for consent-to-adoption.docx while the file still contained literal `[b:...]` markers and stray `]` brackets in its signature blocks; the leak was caught only because the agent happened to eyeball "Keisha Renee Whitfield]" (base1.md:1011-1015) during a structure check. Rule: schema validation is not content verification; re-open each deliverable, extract its text, and scan for build markup before stopping — making the run's lucky catch systematic.

Components deliberately NOT added, per the decision rules:
- No skill: each fixable procedure is 1-3 lines with no recurring multi-step trigger; the runtime already ships the docx skill the run needs.
- No script: the deterministic steps the run hand-rolled (python-docx extraction, marker scanning) succeeded on the first correct attempt — the podman failure was helper selection, not hand-rolled code failing, so it is fixed by guidance, not by a new script.
- No plugin: the ignore-invariant bar (repeated evidence that clear prose is skipped) is not met — one run, no relevant prose existed to skip, and the run did complete both artifacts and re-check them.
- No subagent: no bounded large-input/small-answer subtask recurs in the trajectory.
- systemprompt.md, LongTermMEMORY.md, and the skills/scripts/sub_agents/plugin READMEs are unchanged (inherited as-is).

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
1. NEW skills/adoption-consent-drafting/SKILL.md — practitioner model for consents to adoption and other parental-rights relinquishment instruments, plus the accompanying drafting memorandum (frontmatter name matches directory).

Moments (all from base1):
- Consent ¶9 recites as settled Maryland law a "thirty (30) days" revocation window that "unless the right of revocation is expressly waived in the consent itself" may be waived — then drafts the express waiver as operative text. Memo Rec. 2 doubles down: the waiver "is how her stated wish ... can lawfully be implemented in Maryland." Yet memo Part VI.2 flags only "the current section number" for confirmation. No source in the record states the period's length, start events, or waivability — the sole reference is father's counsel's "the period provided by Maryland law." The run manufactured a specific statutory rule and built the client's core ask on it. SKILL §2 is the decision rule: record window, start events, and waivability from primary law before any operative clause depends on them; if unverified, no express-waiver clause and no memo assurance — draft disclosure plus lawful alternatives (prompt filing/service, in-court execution if verified to matter, finalization calendared outside an unwaived window); §2.3 adds the consistency check the run failed: no operative recital may assert as settled law a proposition another section lists as "to verify."
- Memo Rec. 3 and Part V item 9 assert twice, uncited, "Maryland does not enforce post-adoption contact agreements." SKILL §3: verify the jurisdiction's PACA treatment before advising either way, keep the consent unconditional, and answer the contact question actually asked in the record (Ms. Holloway's May 20 email, including her invitation to coordinate with Ms. Okafor).
- Memo opening: "our clients' sister-in-law's co-parent, Keisha Renee Whitfield" — wrong against the guardianship order (Diana is the child's paternal aunt, the father's sister; Keisha is his never-married former co-parent). SKILL §5 makes the family-map sentence a required memo part, checked clause-by-clause against the court order before finishing.
- SKILL §7 stores the workspace facts the rollout paid to establish, labeled "in this workspace": the case join (adoption 24-A-0001537 / Judge Langford; guardianship 23-G-0004218 / Judge Foss, order entered 8/3/2023; support 19-FS-0008714), the DOB join (intake memo 2018 vs order/home study/counsel letter 2017; BC No. 2017-03-127845 and age/grade corroborate 2017), the intake memo's impossible chronology (dated 3/8/2024 yet reciting events through 4/12/2024), mother's age arithmetic (30, not 31), father's consent executed 3/1/2024 at Jessup with court FILING not confirmed, TANF Oct 2021–Jun 2023 overlapping the ~$14,421 arrears (vs father's counsel's extinguishment claim, contradicted by the guardianship order preserving support), and the express statement that no document in the workspace states the revocation period's terms.
Not encoded as fixes: what base1 already got right (DOB resolution, SSN omission, notary-vs-judge execution recommendation, template-marker cleanup, docx mechanics) — the skill carries rules and verified facts, not corrections the next run would make anyway.

2. systemprompt.md — added the skill's trigger line ("When the task calls for drafting a consent to adoption or another instrument that relinquishes parental rights (with its accompanying drafting memorandum), load the `adoption-consent-drafting` skill before drafting."); a skill exists only once its directory name appears verbatim in always-on text. Paid for by compressing the closing two-sentence paragraph to one line.

3. LongTermMEMORY.md (was empty) — one line: on a conflict in a party's name, date of birth, or identifier, adopt the court-order value in the instrument, corroborate it against a second independent record, and record the conflict and its follow-up in the deliverable. Distilled from the run's DOB-2018-vs-2017 reconciliation: the operation recurs in every instrument task in this practice area, and the intake memo — the losing value — also carried the impossible chronology, marking it the least-reliable layer. Universal rule only; no matter facts stored.

Non-changes: no scripts, plugins, or subagents added — the observed misses are legal-judgment failures (fabricated waivability, uncited enforceability assertion, garbled family map), and base1 already handled docx generation and validation correctly. guardrails.md and tool_guidance.md untouched (KEEP_BASE): no trajectory moment argues for edits there.

kept -> dom1 systemprompt.md trigger line for `adoption-consent-drafting` (closing paragraph compressed to pay for it) -> dom1's first action was loading the skill and its run followed §2 end-to-end (1/1 with trigger); the trigger makes the kept skill fire on every future run instead of depending on the model remembering it.
kept -> dom1 skills/adoption-consent-drafting/SKILL.md body §§1-7 (irrevocability and post-adoption-contact decision rules, required-parts checklists, discrepancy hierarchy, verified workspace facts) -> base1 (1/1) drafted an express waiver of a fabricated "thirty (30) days ... unless expressly waived" revocation right, repeated it in the mother's counsel's certificate, and told the supervising lawyer it was how her wish "can lawfully be implemented" (consent ¶9; memo Rec 2 and §VI.2 — while §VI.2 itself said to confirm the provision), and opened its memo with a garbled "clients' sister-in-law's co-parent" family map (memo line 23); dom1 with the skill: no waiver clause, no length/start/waivability assertion, correct case join and family map, verified-vs-to-verify legal framework.
revised -> dom1 SKILL.md §8 before-finishing checks (+ new check 11: no deliverable may reference the skill, harness, or run) -> dom1's own memo drafting-decisions table leaked the internal phrase "(skill on unverified law)" into the .docx deliverable (1/1), caught only by a round-trip grep and regenerated; the added check targets that leak class directly.
kept -> dom1 LongTermMEMORY.md identity-data hierarchy (1 line) -> the DOB 2018-vs-2017 conflict recurs in every run of this task and base1 resolved it only by ad hoc corroboration; one always-on line generalizes court-order value > independent corroboration > intake memo to every identity conflict in this work type at trivial cost.
Emptiness check: no rollout associated with any kept/revised edit produced nothing — inv1 and dom1 each delivered both requested files, re-opened and validated (leaks: [] / validate.py OK in both).

agg.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: a drafting or advising task where the deliverable must take positions on legal propositions the record raises but cannot verify from primary authority (statutory windows, enforceability regimes, execution formalities), and an unedited run asserts them as settled law.
experience.lesson: encode assertion discipline as decision rules in a task-specific skill (skills/<task>/SKILL.md): forbid operative clauses and advice resting on propositions not verified from primary material; require each such proposition to appear, at the point of use, as flagged-to-verify; and include a consistency check so no later hedge in a companion document cures an unverified operative recital.
experience.evidence: the skills/adoption-consent-drafting/SKILL.md row — non-enforceability of post-adoption contact agreements asserted uncited by both non-carriers (base1 memo:31,116,131; inv1 memo:77) but flagged to-verify by both carriers (dom1 memo:29,148,170; agg1 memo:29,142); base1's fabricated 30-day window and waiver clause (consent:33) against dom1's ¶9 tied to "the period and in the manner provided by Maryland law" (dom1.md:1397).
experience.confidence: medium — the contrast replicates in both directions across four runs, but each candidate is a single rollout on one matter, and inv1's correct handling of the waiver clause without the skill shows the model sometimes self-corrects.

@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+# Guardrails
+
+- Produce artifacts before the budget is at risk. As soon as one deliverable's
+  full content exists, build it, verify it, and get the exact requested
+  filename on disk before investing context in the next. Never leave every
+  requested artifact existing only as an unexecuted script or a plan.
+- A successful write — or a passing `validate.py` — does not establish
+  usability. Schema validation checks OOXML structure, not content: a consent
+  has passed it while still carrying literal `[b:...]` build markers and stray
+  brackets in its signature blocks. Before stopping, re-open each requested
+  deliverable, extract its text, and confirm it parses and carries no build
+  markup or placeholder leaks.
diff -ruN runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/trusts-estates-private-client__draft-consent-to-adoption/harnesses/base/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/trusts-estates-private-client__draft-consent-to-adoption/harnesses/inv1/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md
--- runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/trusts-estates-private-client__draft-consent-to-adoption/harnesses/base/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md	2026-10-25 17:52:39
+++ runs-eight/lab/adapt/lab-oc-agg1/trusts-estates-private-client__draft-consent-to-adoption/harnesses/inv1/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md	2026-10-25 18:05:42
@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+# Tool guidance
+
+## Binary sources and failing helpers
+
+- The `read` tool extracts .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.pdf directly; it is the
+  documented extraction path — do not bypass it for workspace helper scripts.
+  In this workspace `scripts/read_doc.py` defaults to a podman sandbox and
+  podman is not installed, so it fails on every input with
+  `FileNotFoundError: 'podman'`. One missing-binary failure is a missing
+  capability, not bad input: fall back once (to `read`, or to python-docx,
+  which is installed here) and stop — re-running the same helper on the next
+  file fails identically.
+
+## Editing files
+
+- `edit` calls against the same file must be sequential. Several edits to one
+  file issued in a single turn race: all but the last are silently lost even
+  though each reports success. After a batch of edits, re-check the file for
+  the intended changes rather than trusting the per-call confirmations.
+
+## Capped bash output
+
+- When an observation ends with "Full output saved to: <path>", that file
+  contains the complete output; the inline preview is only a prefix. Read the
+  file, with offset, before treating the source as fully read.

+---
+name: adoption-consent-drafting
+description: Practitioner rules for drafting a consent to adoption or other parental-rights relinquishment instrument and its accompanying drafting memorandum — instrument confirmation, irrevocability requests, post-adoption contact, execution formalities, cross-document discrepancy handling, and pre-delivery checks.
+---
+
+# Adoption consent drafting — practitioner model
+
+You are producing a court-filed instrument plus advice to a supervising lawyer.
+Own the legal deliverable, not just text: whose consent, which proceeding,
+which statute, what the instrument may and may not lawfully do, and what the
+supervising lawyer must be told. File formats, validation and output routing
+belong to the harness; this skill governs legal content only.
+
+## 1. Confirm the instrument before drafting
+
+- One instrument per consenting parent. Recite that the other parent's consent
+  is separate and that this consent is independently required.
+- Caption in the adoption case, never the guardianship or support case (see
+  the case join under Verified workspace facts).
+- Identify the statute the sources cite for the proceeding, then verify
+  subtitle and section numbers against current primary law (annotated code,
+  court rules, or an authorised research path) before any operative clause
+  depends on them. Citations appearing in intake memos, reports, and counsel
+  letters are unverified until confirmed.
+- Confirm whose client the consenting parent is and that their counsel is
+  independent of the petitioners (independently retained and paid).
+
+## 2. Decision rule — "make the consent final and irrevocable immediately"
+
+Trigger: a party or client asks for the consent to be irrevocable on signing,
+with no waiting period.
+
+1. Locate the controlling withdrawal/revocation provision and record, with a
+   source: (a) the window's length; (b) its start events (date of execution;
+   any counsel-appointment trigger); (c) whether the statute's own text permits
+   waiving the right inside the consent; (d) whether execution before a judge
+   or magistrate changes revocability.
+2. Only verified propositions become operative recitals. If waivability is not
+   established from primary material or an authorised research path, do NOT
+   draft an express-waiver clause as the mechanism delivering immediate
+   irrevocability, and do NOT tell the supervising lawyer that this is how the
+   wish "can lawfully be implemented." Draft instead: disclosure of the
+   withdrawal right as far as verified; a memo statement of what cannot be
+   promised and why; and the lawful alternatives — prompt filing and service;
+   execution in court if that is verified to matter; calendaring finalization
+   after the window runs (never schedule the finalization hearing inside an
+   unwaived withdrawal window unless verified law permits it).
+3. Consistency check before finishing: no operative clause may assert as
+   settled law a proposition that another section of the deliverables lists as
+   "to verify." Hedging in a later section does not cure an unverified
+   operative recital.
+
+Failure this rule prevents (observed in this workspace's base run): the
+consent recited that the statutory revocation right exists "unless the right
+of revocation is expressly waived in the consent itself," and the memo
+presented the express waiver as the lawful route to the mother's wish — while
+the same memo's legal-framework section said to confirm the
+revocation/waiver provision. Nothing in the record establishes the period's
+length, start events, or waivability. An invalid waiver clause invites a
+post-placement collateral attack — the most expensive failure in this work.
+
+## 3. Decision rule — post-adoption contact / visitation
+
+Trigger: any question whether a contact arrangement belongs "in the adoption
+papers" or in the consent.
+
+- Keep the consent unconditional. A consent conditioned on promised future
+  contact is vulnerable to invalidation for inducement or condition.
+- Verify this jurisdiction's treatment of post-adoption contact agreements
+  from primary material before advising; do not assert enforceability OR
+  non-enforceability without a source.
+- If the understanding is documented at all, it goes in a separate instrument
+  whose binding effect is stated expressly per verified law; recommend
+  coordinating with the consenting parent's counsel.
+- Check whether an existing guardianship order grants contact rights; those
+  end with the adoption — say so in the memo.
+- The memo must answer the actual question asked in the record (who asked,
+  in which document), including any invitation to coordinate with the other
+  side's counsel.
+
+## 4. Consent — required parts (check each)
+
+Caption block: court, adoption caption, adoption case number, instrument title
+naming the consenting parent.
+
+Recitals, in order: (1) consenting parent identified — name, date of birth,
+address, adult status, relationship to the child; (2) child identified — name,
+date of birth, place of birth, birth-certificate number; no Social Security
+number or other unnecessary identifier; (3) adoptive parents identified,
+including each one's relationship to the child and to each other; (4) pending
+proceeding — petition, case number, judge, and the live guardianship order by
+case number; (5) the other parent's separate consent recited with its
+execution details as known, expressly not a substitute for this one; (6)
+independent counsel — name, firm, address, retained and paid solely by the
+consenting parent; advice on rights including withdrawal; receipt of an
+executed copy; (7) consequences in plain language — which rights end (custody,
+visitation and contact, decision-making), who the legal parents become, that
+the effect is permanent; (8) voluntariness, no coercion, no payment or
+inducement by anyone, and capacity — with known history (e.g., treatment and
+recovery) affirmatively disclosed rather than omitted; (9) the withdrawal
+right handled per §2; (10) consent to adoption by the named petitioners and
+request for the decree; any notice waiver only "to the extent permitted by
+law"; (11) an unconditionality clause per §3; (12) verification/declaration
+of truthfulness.
+
+Execution apparatus: execution date line; consenting parent's signature block
+with name and address; counsel approval/certificate block; two disinterested
+witnesses; a notary acknowledgment block WITH an alternative for execution
+before a judge, magistrate, or other officer authorised by statute to take
+consents — and resolve from the statute, before the signing is scheduled,
+which officers the law actually authorises.
+

+
+(1) TO/FROM/DATE/RE, privilege line, matter number. (2) Assignment in one
+paragraph, including the family map stated correctly in plain words — e.g.
+"petitioner X is the child's paternal aunt, sister of the biological father;
+the consenting mother and the father were never married" — then check each
+clause of that sentence against the court order's findings before finishing
+(the base run here opened with a garbled "clients' sister-in-law's
+co-parent"). (3) Numbered recommendations, each traceable to a source or
+flagged as inference. (4) Parties/counsel/proceedings table with sources.
+(5) Source-document list. (6) Drafting decisions keyed to the consent's
+paragraphs. (7) A discrepancy log — one row per conflict: number, conflict,
+treatment adopted, follow-up — covering every conflict found however small,
+plus a list of key identifiers verified consistent. (8) Legal framework
+separating verified citations from to-verify items at the point of use.
+(9) Execution logistics — officer identity, attendees (the consenting
+parent's counsel present so the certificate is contemporaneous), when the
+draft goes to that counsel (calendar any review window they asked for), what
+gets filed afterward. (10) Open items with owners and dates. (11) Limitations.
+
+Separation discipline throughout: label what is source text, matter fact,
+legal inference, risk assessment, and recommendation — never present one as
+another.
+

+numbers): court-order findings > executed or notarized instruments and counsel
+confirmations > professional reports (home studies) > intake memoranda >

+certificate-number year against date of birth; stated age or school grade
+against date of birth; arithmetic of ages against stated dates). Every
+conflict is logged even when resolved, and a resolved conflict still gets a
+follow-up (obtain the certified record; correct the internal file).

+parent's relinquishment "resolves all obligations related to the child" does

+existing support order is expressly preserved by a court order, and whether
+public-assistance benefits paid during part of the arrears period (e.g., TANF)
+create an assigned State claim for the overlap.
+

+  or captions between these cases.
+- Child DOB join: the intake memo (sections 3 and 5) says born March 17, 2018;
+  the guardianship order, the home study, and the father's counsel's letter
+  say March 17, 2017; Birth Certificate No. 2017-03-127845 and the memo's own

+  instrument; log the conflict; follow up for the certified certificate.

+  2024 (petition filed March 20; home study completed April 12) — an
+  impossible chronology; the later-dated facts are the corroborated ones.
+- Mother: Keisha Renee Whitfield, DOB September 2, 1993 (sources calling her
+  "31" are off — she is 30 until September 2, 2024); the instrument uses date
+  of birth only. Counsel Danica Okafor, Esq. (MD Bar No. 1104582),
+  independently retained; she asked for the draft at least one week before a

+  consent remains in effect and on file with the court.

+   background.

+8. The family-map sentence is correct against the court order.
+9. Arrears and benefit-assignment issues addressed as advocacy-versus-law.
+10. Both requested files produced; signature, witness, notary/officer blocks
+    complete and coherent.

+# Guardrails
+
+- Produce artifacts before the budget is at risk. As soon as one deliverable's
+  full content exists, build it, verify it, and get the exact requested
+  filename on disk before investing context in the next. Never leave every
+  requested artifact existing only as an unexecuted script or a plan.
+- A successful write — or a passing `validate.py` — does not establish
+  usability. Schema validation checks OOXML structure, not content: a consent
+  has passed it while still carrying literal `[b:...]` build markers and stray
+  brackets in its signature blocks. Before stopping, re-open each requested
+  deliverable, extract its text, and confirm it parses and carries no build
+  markup or placeholder leaks.

+# Tool guidance
+
+## Binary sources and failing helpers
+
+- The `read` tool extracts .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.pdf directly; it is the
+  documented extraction path — do not bypass it for workspace helper scripts.
+  In this workspace `scripts/read_doc.py` defaults to a podman sandbox and
+  podman is not installed, so it fails on every input with
+  `FileNotFoundError: 'podman'`. One missing-binary failure is a missing
+  capability, not bad input: fall back once (to `read`, or to python-docx,
+  which is installed here) and stop — re-running the same helper on the next
+  file fails identically.
+
+## Editing files
+
+- `edit` calls against the same file must be sequential. Several edits to one
+  file issued in a single turn race: all but the last are silently lost even
+  though each reports success. After a batch of edits, re-check the file for
+  the intended changes rather than trusting the per-call confirmations.
+
+## Capped bash output
+
+- When an observation ends with "Full output saved to: <path>", that file
+  contains the complete output; the inline preview is only a prefix. Read the
+  file, with offset, before treating the source as fully read.
